subject: drama
topicName: Performing a Character from a Script

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Actioning: assigning a transitive verb to each line — 'I WARN', 'I BEG', 'I THREATEN' — gives every line a purpose and energy.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Vocal skills: pace, pitch, pause, volume, tone, emphasis, accent — each must be chosen deliberately for character and situation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Physical skills: posture, gesture, facial expression, proxemics, eye contact, movement — the body communicates as much as the voice.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Line learning: learn lines EARLY so you can focus on delivery, not recall. Learn intention, not just words.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain what actioning is and how it helps an actor deliver lines more effectively. | Describe the vocal and physical skills you would use to perform a character experiencing a crisis of confidence. | How can an actor maintain truthfulness in performance without simply 'acting' emotions?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Actioning assigns a transitive verb to each line (I CONVINCE, I INTIMIDATE, I PLEAD). It gives every line a purpose, prevents flat delivery, and ensures the actor is always DOING something to the othe | Vocal: quieter volume, hesitant pace, rising pitch on questions, long pauses before responses. Physical: closed posture, avoiding eye contact, fidgeting hands, retreating spatially. Each choice justif | Truthfulness comes from understanding what the character WANTS and pursuing it honestly, not from pretending to feel emotions. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Actioning verbs must be TRANSITIVE (done TO someone): I WARN, not 'I am angry' Always link vocal/physical choices to CHARACTER MOTIVATION Performing for an examiner: confidence, energy, projection and focus from the start Never describe emotions — describe the ACTIONS that show the emotions
